name: Antisymmetric / hierarchical two-head architecture (related-vs-NEGATIVE_OTHER gate + reversal-equivariant direction head)
links: Task spec and scorer definitions: https://inigolopezgazpio.net/SemEval-2027-Task-2-DiCo-NLI/ ; pilot paper (LREC 2026, Apaolaza Larraya et al., 'Assessing Logical Coherence of LLMs via Fine-Grained NLI'): https://lrec.elra.info/lrec2026-main-423 ; closest prior art for order-(anti)symmetry constraints in NLI: Li et al. 2019 'A Logic-Driven Framework for Consistency of Neural Models' (EMNLP, arXiv:1909.00126, code github.com/utahnlp/consistency); Minervini & Riedel 2018 'Adversarially Regularising Neural NLI Models to Integrate Logical Background Knowledge' (ACL); antisymmetric pairwise scoring s(a,b) = g(a,b) - g(b,a) follows the RankNet / Bradley-Terry pairwise-preference construction. No off-the-shelf HF checkpoint: it is a custom head on top of any cross-encoder (DeBERTa-v3, mDeBERTa-v3, XLM-R, mmBERT). In-repo anchor: src/labels.py REVERSE_PERM = (0, 2, 1, 3).
year: Design pattern (2016-2019 roots in pairwise ranking and logic-constrained NLI); proposed here for DiCo-NLI 2026-2027
license_access: Method only, no license constraints; inherits the license of the chosen backbone (e.g. MIT for DeBERTa-v3 / mDeBERTa-v3, MIT for XLM-R). Fully open-weight compatible.
track_coverage: All four tracks (T1 EN, T2 ES, T3 EU, T4 mixed). It is language-agnostic: it only needs the ability to run the encoder on both orders (a,b) and (b,a), which every track provides because each reversible item's twin is in the same file. In T4 the swap also swaps languages (en-es original <-> es-en flipped), which the construction handles automatically.
basque_quality: Not applicable to the method itself; Basque competence comes entirely from the backbone (e.g. XLM-R-large or mmBERT or a Basque encoder). The architecture neither helps nor hurts Basque lexical coverage, but its parameter tying (one direction head shared across both orders) halves the effective hypothesis space, which should help most where data/pretraining are weakest (EU) [uncertain].
cross_lingual_robustness: Guarantee holds per input pair regardless of language mix, so T4 mixed pairs get exactly the same consistency guarantee as monolingual ones. It does not by itself close the accuracy gap between monolingual and mixed inputs (that gap comes from the encoder's cross-lingual alignment); combine with cross-lingual view aggregation or cross-lingual consistency KL for that.
architecture: Two coupled heads on a shared cross-encoder E. Run E on both orders: h_ab = E([CLS] a [SEP] b), h_ba = E([CLS] b [SEP] a). (1) Relatedness gate (symmetric): r = w_r . (h_ab + h_ba) / 2 -> p(NEG | a,b) = sigmoid(-r), identical for both orders. (2) Direction head (antisymmetric): scalar d(a,b) = g(h_ab) - g(h_ba), so d(b,a) = -d(a,b); equivalence logit e(a,b) = u(h_ab) + u(h_ba) (symmetric). Conditional 3-way softmax over related labels with logits [e, +d, -d] for [EQ, FE, BE]. Final: p(EQ) = (1 - p_NEG) * softmax_EQ, p(FE) = (1 - p_NEG) * softmax_FE, etc. This yields exactly p(FE|a,b) = p(BE|b,a), p(EQ|a,b) = p(EQ|b,a), p(NEG|a,b) = p(NEG|b,a), i.e. p(b,a) = p(a,b)[REVERSE_PERM]. A simpler equivalent variant is 'symmetrised logits': z_sym(a,b) = 0.5 * (z(a,b) + z(b,a)[REVERSE_PERM]) using a standard 4-way head, trained end-to-end on the symmetrised output. Hierarchical training loss: BCE on related-vs-NEG for all rows + CE on the 3-way direction softmax for reversible rows only (so NEG rows do not pollute the direction head), optional class weights.
params: Backbone parameters only (e.g. 184M DeBERTa-v3-base, 435M DeBERTa-v3-large, 278M mDeBERTa-v3-base, 560M XLM-R-large) plus a few thousand head parameters (two or three linear layers of size hidden_dim).
compute: Two encoder forward passes per training example (or, equivalently, batching the twin pair together, which the data already provides), so roughly 2x FLOPs of a vanilla single-order classifier per unique source pair, but no extra examples are needed since reversed twins are already in the training files. Sequences are very short (phrase pairs, typically < 32 tokens), so base models fine-tune in minutes and large models (435-560M) in well under an hour on one 24 GB GPU; no multi-GPU needed.
sample_efficiency: Favourable for ~1.3k reversible source pairs (T1 train: 2564 reversible rows = 1282 twins + 478 NEG singletons): tying removes the need to learn FE/BE separately and makes the reversed twin a free, noise-free second supervision signal on the same parameters. Analogy: Li et al. 2019 show that mirrored-instance symmetry constraints mostly reduce inconsistency without accuracy loss even at 1-5% of SNLI/MNLI; Asai & Hajishirzi 2020 report the largest consistency gains in low-data regimes. Seed variance on such small data remains substantial (expect +-1-2 F1 across seeds) and should be handled with fold/seed ensembling [uncertain].
reported_results: No published results for this exact architecture on DiCo-NLI or PhrasIS. Related evidence: (a) Li et al. 2019 (BERT-base, SNLI+MNLI 100%): symmetry violation rho_S drops from 18.1% to 6.2% with mirrored-instance loss (1.1-1.4% with extra unlabeled pairs), while test accuracy is unchanged (SNLI 90.1 -> 90.2-90.5, MNLI 83.5 -> 84.1-84.3); at 5% data rho_S 25.3% -> 3.2-7.1% with accuracy 84.6 -> 85.3-85.4 (SNLI). (b) Asai & Hajishirzi 2020: symmetric data augmentation + consistency regularisation cuts symmetric violations on WIQA from 13.9% to 8.3% and improves accuracy by +1 to +5 points; +12-14 points with 20% of the data. (c) Pilot DiCo baseline without any consistency mechanism: DeBERTa-v3-base 0.75 W-F1 / 0.84 SoftCons / 0.79 HardCons. The architectural approach enforces what those soft methods only approximate, so SoftCons on gold-reversible pairs predicted as reversible labels becomes 1.0 by construction.
pilot_dico_results: Not evaluated in the LREC 2026 pilot, which only benchmarked vanilla fine-tuned encoder, decoder and encoder-decoder models without consistency-enforcing components (best: DeBERTa-v3-base 0.75 / 0.84 / 0.79 on the English positive combined track; encoder family mean 0.713 / 0.770 / 0.721).
negative_other_handling: Decided by the symmetric relatedness gate p(NEG) = sigmoid(-r), shared by both orders, with a tunable threshold (tune on dev for weighted F1). Yes, it can emit NEGATIVE_OTHER on a gold-reversible pair; when it does, it emits NEG for both twins (the gate is symmetric), so the pair is never direction-inconsistent but loses HardCons for that pair. Whether the official scorer counts a NEG/NEG prediction on a gold-reversible pair as SoftCons-consistent is not documented (Rev is defined only over EQ/FE/BE) [uncertain]. NEG items are singletons in train/dev, so the gate is trained on (a,b) only; symmetric augmentation (b,a) -> NEG is safe because PhrasIS non-reversible relations (similar/related/opposite/unrelated) are order-invariant [uncertain].
metric_tradeoff: SoftCons: pushed to ~1.0 on pairs predicted as reversible (ties aside), the maximum achievable. HardCons: rises toward item accuracy on reversible pairs, because errors now come in coherent pairs rather than one-sided; expect HardCons gain larger than W-F1 gain. Weighted F1: roughly neutral to slightly positive (tying acts as regularisation; symmetrisation averages two noisy views); a risk is small loss if the direction head's antisymmetry fights order-specific surface cues that were genuinely predictive, and a mis-tuned NEG gate can cost F1 on the 16% NEG class.
integration: Custom nn.Module wrapping AutoModel (not AutoModelForSequenceClassification): encode (a,b) and (b,a) in one batch (the twin rows already exist; for NEG singletons, synthesize the swap), compute gate + direction head, return 4-way log-probs in LABELS order. Minimal version: keep AutoModelForSequenceClassification with 4 labels and add a symmetrisation wrapper z_sym = 0.5*(z_ab + z_ba[..., REVERSE_PERM]) used in both training loss and inference (a few lines using src/labels.py REVERSE_PERM). Dataloader must group twins by reverse_instance_id(). Loss: hierarchical BCE+CE or plain CE on the symmetrised 4-way distribution.
ensemble_compatibility: Yes: produces proper 4-way probability vectors that already satisfy p(b,a) = Rev(p(a,b)); averaging several such models (or log-prob pooling across views) preserves the property, so it plugs directly into joint decoding and cross-lingual view pooling. Calibrate with temperature scaling on dev.
inference_cost: 2 forward passes per ordered pair, but each twin pair shares them, so total cost equals one pass per test row: ~4k rows per monolingual track (~24k for T4 if similar scale) of < 32 tokens takes seconds to a few minutes on one GPU even for large backbones.
rules_disclosure: Pure modeling choice; no external data. Disclose as encoder-only (or the backbone's family), open-weight, fine-tuned, custom reversal-equivariant head; note that the system uses the pairing of each test item with its reversed twin (derived from instance_id / by swapping the two phrases), which is allowed input-level information but should be stated. Self-constructing the swapped input needs no metadata at all, so rule risk is low.
contamination: Method introduces no data; contamination depends on the backbone and any PhrasIS/iSTS pretraining data used. No additional risk.
structural_cue_dependence: Low. Only needs the two phrases, which it can swap itself; does not require pair_id, twin ids, or singleton heuristics. If test metadata changes, it still works (it simply runs both orders internally).
priority: P1 (the cheap symmetrised-logits variant is effectively P0 and should be part of the first strong baseline; the full hierarchical gate+direction head is P1)
expected_gain: Relative to an unconstrained DeBERTa-style baseline (pilot 0.75 / 0.84 / 0.79): SoftCons +0.10-0.16 (to ~0.95-1.0 over gold-reversible pairs, limited only by NEG predictions), HardCons +0.02-0.06, W-F1 0 to +0.02 [uncertain]. Gains overlap heavily with joint pair decoding (which gives the same guarantee at inference time); the architectural version adds value by also training the shared representation to be reversal-equivariant and by separating the NEG decision from direction, which makes NEG-threshold tuning cleaner.
